Hi Ariella / Lumina contracts team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a clean draft of the Security Exhibit (Security-Exhibit-Draft_v3.docx) plus a one-page evidence cadence summary. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm SOC 2 report delivery window (we can provide annual and point-in-time if helpful)
- Confirm preferred pen-test notice window (we propose a 30-day notice and a 7-day staging access window)
- Order form redline: we want to add an "inspection-lite" option that clarifies sample sizes and scope for standard accounts (helps reduce evidence volume for smaller teams)

Ben and Lauren are copied for ops/legal alignment. Proposed timeline: get redline notes from Lumina legal by EOD Wednesday 12/17 so we can propose an MSA change package for internal GC review on Thursday.

Attachments: [Attachment: Security-Exhibit-Draft_v3.docx] [Attachment: evidence-cadence-summary.pdf]

Next steps / ask from you: please flag any items that are unacceptable or need alternative language; call out any required audit rights beyond SOC 2 / ISO reports (e.g., privileged inspection).

Best,

From: Ariella Mendez <ariella.mendez@luminahealth.com>

Cc: contracts@luminahealth.com, security@luminahealth.com
Date: 2027-12-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: evidence cadence proposal + MSA/order-form redline priorities

Vanessa,

Thanks for sending — useful start. A couple of clarifying q's from Lumina legal/security:

1) SOC 2: we can accept the annual Type II report but need a statement on the lookback period. Can Redwood confirm last audit end date and whether there are interim controls or bridging letters?

2) Pen test: proposed 30-day notice is fine, but our procurement requires at least one full week of staging access (baselined) and a defined access window. Can you confirm what you mean by "staging access window"?

3) Evidence cadence: the "inspection-lite" concept looks promising; need an explicit sampling matrix and acceptance criteria. Can you provide the sizes / bands by customer tier?

We're looping in security@luminahealth.com for technical confirmation. Contractually, please send redlineable Word for the exhibit and call out any non-negotiable audit rights (e.g., privileged inspection for escalations).

Ariella Mendez
Sr. Contracts Manager, Lumina Health
ariella.mendez@luminahealth.com

Subject: Re: Security exhibit: evidence cadence proposal + MSA/order-form redline priorities

Looping in operational detail so we can give Lumina concrete bands:

- SOC 2: Last Type II covered period ended 2027-06-30. We can provide a bridging letter for controls after that date; our security eng can also provide a one-page control snapshot on request.

- Pen test: by "staging access window" I mean a dedicated test environment with a pre-approved IP allowlist and a 5-7 day window where our on-call runbook is in "test mode" (shorter response SLOs, test-user accounts). We generally recommend 7 days to accommodate remediation discovery.

- Sampling matrix (proposed): 
  * Small customers (<$10k ARR): inspection-lite — sample 5 hosts / 1 release window
  * Mid customers ($10k-$200k ARR): 10 hosts / 2 release windows or one 7-day test window
  * Enterprise (>$200k ARR): full K/V sampling + privileged inspection option on request

I've attached a matrix (pen-test-access-matrix.xlsx) and a quick summary pdf. If Lumina wants more granular bands we can expand.

Attachments: [Attachment: pen-test-access-matrix.xlsx] [Attachment: evidence-cadence-summary.pdf]

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Security Ops (Contracts Support)
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ariella Mendez <ariella.mendez@luminahealth.com>, contracts@luminahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-15T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: evidence cadence proposal + MSA/order-form redline priorities

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround, Ariella and team. Summary / proposed next steps: 

1) Redwood will add the SOC 2 last-audit date and an optional bridging statement paragraph to the exhibit.
2) We'll explicitly define the pen-test staging access as "7-day test window, dedicated staging, pre-approved IP allowlist" and publish the runbook excerpt in the exhibit appendix.
3) We'll add the sampling bands Ben proposed into an "Inspection Options" table and make the default the inspection-lite for non-enterprise order forms.
4) We will label the enterprise privileged inspection as "by mutual agreement" and include a one-sentence remediation escalation flow (timebox + confidentiality guardrails).

Ask: Ariella — if you can mark any of the above as unacceptable or propose alternate language by 12/17 EOD, we'll prepare a redline-ready Word and route to our GC. If we don't hear back by then we'll assume Lumina agrees to the above defaults and will package the MSA + order form redline for signature draft.

Shared draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-Redwood-Lumina-Exhibit (see Security-Exhibit-Draft_v3.docx)

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts

Subject: Re: Security exhibit: evidence cadence proposal + MSA/order-form redline priorities

Vanessa / Ben / Lauren,

Appreciate the detail — Lumina legal concurs with the proposed structure but requests two edits before we sign off to route to procurement: 

1) Add explicit language under Order Form options that "inspection-lite" excludes privileged inspection and any manual live-memory sampling unless specifically elected by customer.
2) Clarify that pen-test staging access windows will be scheduled with at least 7 days' notice and that Redwood will provide an IP allowlist and a point-of-contact for on-call support during the window.

We'll incorporate these edits and send a marked redline Word back to you by EOD 12/17. Regarding the MSA: procurement will need the revised Order Form + Security Exhibit attached to the signature package; please include a final invoice/PO instruction line in the order form (we typically need a 60-day billing window).

We will review the DocuSign packet once it's shared.

Thanks,
Lumina Contracts
[contracts@luminahealth.com]
